beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Rich for about a minute. Five bites come out of that pay first. Whatever survives is the only part that grows.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Bite one is tax. 22% of his pay goes to tax before it reaches him. $1,100 gone.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Bite two, my rent. $1,500 for a tiny apartment with a view of another apartment.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Bite three is the car. The loan, the gas and the insurance come to $600 a month.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Bite four is food. Groceries, plus takeout way too many nights. $600.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Bite five is fun. His phone, streaming, nights out: $700. In total, $4,500 is spent.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Hold on. Out of my $5,000 pay, what's even left for me?

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Here's the catch. The $500 that survives is the only money that can grow.

beats.speaker: priya
beats.say: Invested every month at an assumed 7% for 30 years, that little pile becomes $613,544.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Fine. It starts on my next payday.
